charts.title: v2ecoli vs Beulig 2025 batch-phase biomass-density gap (preliminary)
charts.caption: Final biomass concentration (g/L) from existing mbp-02 multigen runs at cpa ∈ {1, 1e6, 1e9}, overlaid against Beulig 2025 batch-phase target band (50-80 g/L). Star marks the cpa that would close the residual gap at the current 2-gen / 60-sim-min batch duration: ~2e+13.
charts.interpretation: cpa=1 (literal single-cell) reaches ~3.3e-12 g/L at t=2-gen. cpa=1e9 (Beulig-regime representative-sampling) reaches ~3.3e-03 g/L — still 4.2 orders below Beulig's stated 50-80 g/L target. The residual gap is NOT a cpa-scaling problem (cpa is exact, see chart 04 variance bands); it's a BATCH-DURATION problem. v2ecoli's current 60-sim-min / 2-gen runs are far short of Beulig's ~6 h batch phase. Closing the gap requires (a) longer batch duration to accumulate more cell mass per agent, (b) cpa ~ 2e+13 (near Avogadro-mol scale — likely impractical), OR (c) fed-batch operations (deferred upstream blocker, pbg-bioreactor-transport-fork). mbp-05's comparison harness can render this gap explicitly BEFORE evaluating whether v2ecoli's biology reproduces Beulig's trajectory — diagnostic-first, evaluative-second.

charts.title: Biomass trajectories (cpa=1/1e6/1e9) vs Beulig 2025 batch endpoint
charts.caption: log-y population.biomass_concentration_gL(t) for cpa ∈ {1, 1e6, 1e9} v2ecoli runs alongside Beulig 2025's batch-phase endpoint band at t=6h. Time-series counterpart to chart 00.
charts.interpretation: Visual rendering of the 4-5 order density-gap at the same time-axis as Beulig's batch endpoint. v2ecoli's 60-min trajectories end far below Beulig's 6-h endpoint band, and the slopes don't suggest the gap would close with a 6x duration extension — per-cell mass plateaus after ~1 generation in the M9-glucose calibration regime. Closing the gap needs the architectural moves listed in chart 00's meta (longer duration via fed-batch / impossibly-large cpa / candidate surrogate engine in mbp-06).

The 175-min run confirms v2ecoli's biomass plateaus around 4.3 mg/L per division cycle, NOT because duration is short but because single_daughters caps total biomass at cell_mass × cpa for one lineage.

Beulig: DDB_PD_006_AMBR_R9, DDB_PD_009_AMBR_R10, DDB_PD_009_AMBR_R11, DDB_PD_006_AMBR_R8, DDB_PD_038_AMBR_R10 from reactor_OD_data.csv, batch phase only.
charts.interpretation:
This chart settles the architectural question conclusively. v2ecoli at cpa=1e9 plateaus around 4.3 mg/L over 175 sim-min — the trajectory oscillates between ~1 and ~4 mg/L following the division cycle (cell_mass 1100→2300 fg → halve at division), but does NOT accumulate across generations. The single_daughters convention follows ONE lineage; biomass = cell_mass × cpa is bounded by the cell's mass range. Beulig batch peaks at ~9.6 g/L — 3.3 orders above v2ecoli's plateau. Closing this gap requires either: (a) a population composite that tracks accumulating cell count (counter to single_daughters), (b) impossibly-large cpa (~1e12), or (c) fed-batch + surrogate engine (mbp-06 candidate-future-study). mbp-05's comparison harness will surface this diagnostically rather than try to close it via tuning.

[2026-05-29 CAVEAT — single_daughters configuration]: This chart's plateau finding is empirically valid FOR the single_daughters configuration (one daughter followed at each division — the v2ecoli default). The architectural-cap statement is overstated as a blanket claim: with both daughters tracked (--no-single-daughters), v2ecoli's population doubles every generation and biomass DOES accumulate exponentially. The follow-up run aggregator-cpa1e9-multigen --no-single-daughters tests this directly; see chart 03 (companion). The 3.3-order single_daughters plateau gap may be reduced to ~1.2 orders under both_daughters, though full closure to Beulig batch (~9.6 g/L) still requires fed-batch operations + the architectural decisions in mbp-06.

charts.interpretation:
REVISES chart-02's architectural-cap framing with EMPIRICAL evidence. The both-daughters run peaks at 4.39 mg/L (Δ +2.1% vs single_daughters' 4.31 mg/L). The runner's INTERNAL log line `gen 2 → following agent '00' at tick 2501` reveals the root cause: `run_multigen_parquet` (v2ecoli.library.parquet_run) simulates BOTH daughters at division moments but then follows ONE lineage for continued simulation + parquet emission. So `--no-single-daughters` flips the COMPOSITE-LEVEL division behavior but doesn't change the runner's emit pattern, and the plateau persists. The chart 02 architectural claim about single_daughters capping biomass at cell_mass × cpa is true for OBSERVED biomass but the actual root cause is the runner's lineage-emit logic, NOT the single_daughters config alone.

For TRUE both-daughters accumulation (2^N cells after N gens), v2ecoli needs a fundamentally different runner that simulates all agents in parallel — neither single_daughters=True/False in the current run_multigen_parquet path produces it. This is itself an architectural finding for mbp-06: 'population composite runner' as a candidate-future-study, distinct from the single_daughters lineage convention. Closing the Beulig batch gap (~9.6 g/L) still requires fed-batch + that population-runner architecture, not just a config flip.
